The core innovation lies in the integration of a video tokenizer, which converts continuous image sequences into discrete tokens, and a camera encoder, which transforms camera trajectories into 3D positional guidance. The method leverages a permuted spatial structure within the transformer to enhance the understanding of spatial relationships while maintaining temporal consistency. The authors demonstrate that ARSS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the RealEstate10K and ACID datasets, and also show promising results in zero-shot novel view synthesis on the DL3DV-10K benchmark. The paper provides extensive experimental results and ablation studies, but several key areas need further investigation and clarification to fully understand the strengths and limitations of the proposed method. The reliance on a pre-trained video tokenizer, the lack of detailed architectural specifications, and the absence of a comprehensive analysis of computational efficiency and scalability are notable concerns. This approach not only aligns well with the autoregressive nature of the problem but also demonstrates the potential of transformer architectures in generating high-quality, temporally consistent novel views. Secondly, the introduction of a camera encoder that converts camera trajectories into 3D positional guidance using Plücker raymaps is a creative solution. Despite the paper's strengths, several limitations and concerns need to be addressed to fully validate the proposed method. One of the primary concerns is the reliance on a pre-trained video tokenizer, which limits the novelty of the approach.
